# Bug: LongestCommonSubsequence fails with UnboundLocalError

I was trying to use the LongestCommonSubsequence class to calculate the similarity between two strings, but I'm getting an error when running my code.

## Reproduction steps

```python
from strsimpy.longest_common_subsequence import LongestCommonSubsequence

lcs = LongestCommonSubsequence()
s1 = "hello"
s2 = "world"
result = lcs.length(s1, s2)  # This raises an error
```

## Actual outcome

When trying to calculate the length of the longest common subsequence, I get the following error:

```
UnboundLocalError: local variable 's0_len' referenced before assignment
```

The same error occurs when using the `distance` method as well, since it internally calls the `length` method.

## Expected outcome

The method should correctly calculate and return the length of the longest common subsequence between the two strings without raising any errors.

## Additional information

I noticed this happens with any pair of strings I try to compare. The error seems to be related to variable initialization order in the `length` method.

## Environment

- Python version: 3.10
- strsimpy version: latest from pip
